Where it began

Michael Bracewell was born in Masterton on 14 February 1991 and went to school at Kavanagh College in Dunedin. Cricket was very much the family business. His uncles Brendon and John Bracewell both played Test cricket for New Zealand, and his cousin Doug went on to play for his country too.

Not every Bracewell took up a bat, mind. His cousin Melanie made her name as a comedian, which suggests family gatherings were never short of either runs or laughs.

The player

He played his domestic cricket for Wellington, who gave him a contract in 2018. In March 2020, in a Plunket Shield match, he collected five wickets in a first-class innings for the first time. Then, in January 2022, he hammered an unbeaten 141 for the Wellington Firebirds in a Super Smash game against the Central Stags. At the time no one had made a bigger score in a Twenty20 match in New Zealand.

Two months later he was in the New Zealand side. He made his one-day debut against the Netherlands in March 2022 and his Test debut against England in June. In 10 Tests between 2022 and 2025 he scored 339 runs at 21.19, with a best of 74 not out, took 25 wickets and held 14 catches.

What made him special

He was the kind of cricketer captains love: useful in every part of the game. He could bat low in the order, bowl a few overs and take a catch. In January 2023 he made a one-day hundred against India that was, at the time, the third-fastest by a New Zealander. It also made him only the second batter, after MS Dhoni, with more than one one-day century from number seven or lower.

In Tests his wickets came at a cost, at 47.92 runs apiece, and a Test hundred never quite arrived, with that unbeaten 74 the closest he came. His best bowling of 4 for 75 shows what he could do on his day.

A summer to remember

The middle of 2022 was quite a stretch. In July he made his first one-day century, against Ireland. He made his T20 international debut against the same opponents on 18 July, and two days later he took a hat-trick with the very first over he bowled in that format. Most bowlers spend a whole career waiting for one of those.

And finally

He was thirty-one when he first played for New Zealand, an age when some cricketers are starting to think about what comes next. Instead he went on to join Royal Challengers Bangalore in the 2023 IPL and was picked for the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 Champions Trophy. For a late starter, he kept up a fair pace.
